articles.title: Despite the teething issues, Dyson’s Camerajet toothbrush packs in a lot of clever tech – but is it worth £420?
articles.summary: Dyson’s first electric toothbrush watches you brush and flosses for you, but there are far cheaper ways to get an effective clean. • The best electric toothbrushes for every budget.
body: When Dyson announced it was entering the toothbrush market, the world responded almost as one: “Four hundred and twenty pounds? For a toothbrush!?”

No, it wasn’t a stray decimal point – or if it was, Dyson is doubling down and leaning into the mistake. Unlike high-end brushes from Oral-B or Philips Sonicare, where the “recommended” in “recommended retail price” is doing a heroic amount of heavy lifting given the frequent discounts, the Dyson CameraJet will actually set you back £419.99.

The CameraJet is an electric toothbrush and a water flosser, so if you were being charitable – or merely looking for a way to justify the cost to yourself – you could call this two for the price of one on the best electric toothbrushes and water flossers.

There’s a lot of clever technology here, and Dyson’s commitment to doing something different should be applauded, even if it’s just to give your hands something to do besides reaching for your credit card.

articles.title: AI has come for Arizona’s water
articles.summary: A hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites.
body: I stand before the savior of Arizona’s economy. Like all great deities, it demands sacrifice. In the desert, nothing is more precious than water, and water is what must be given — nearly 5 million gallons a day, every day, sourced from Phoenix’s municipal supply. The offering has been well worth it.

All of this is the fruit of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading producer of microchips. Its Arizona operation is the result of a pre-pandemic gamble Phoenix made to revive its sluggish economy, which never quite rebounded from the Great Recession. Now TSMC’s foundry looms over the city’s outskirts.
Now the state has a sixth C, Arizona native Christine Mackay tells me. “Chips.”

articles.title: I Did Push-Ups With Snap’s Chunky AR Glasses
articles.summary: They fit better than they look and stay put when you move, but Snap’s $2,195 Specs still feel like a developer prototype in search of a purpose.
body: I hadn’t expected to be doing augmented reality push-ups in the middle of the mall. Yet there I was, wearing bulky Snap Specs while facing the ground.

The Lens (what Snap calls apps on its augmented reality headset ) is called Thirty Ups. It is in Halloween mode now, so when I look down, a virtual cartoon Jack-o’-lantern sits right next to where I’m supposed to start working out. I’m not trying to get jacked right now, but my goal is to see if these gigantic smart glasses will fall off when I’m staring straight down and moving up and down.

I get into position and start my workout. When I go down and back up, a little virtual circle on the ground below me starts counting up. I don’t get to 30 push-ups. I’m surrounded by people, many of whom are now staring at me, and it feels too hot outside to keep going without feeling gross. I get in 12 reps before giving up. The glasses only count 11 because it tells me I “skipped” one. Great.
The nearby Snap representative is thrilled. “You’re the first person who’s tried that one,” he says. I’m also pleasantly surprised. These glasses seem huge, but they stayed on my face just fine.

articles.title: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
articles.summary: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.
body: So says my iPhone screen, where Death Clock, an AI -powered longevity app that predicts life expectancy based on your medical habits and lifestyle, has produced an image of a smiling grim reaper to celebrate my expiration date. There he was one September morning, looking especially thrilled about the reveal, gesturing with a peace sign as he reclined in a doughnut-shaped pool inflatable under that giant number: 74.

I have never resented getting older, but I suppose that’s younger than I’d like to be when my time is up. In the last four years—years that brought the passing of my grandmother and aunt within 18 months—I’ve become hyperaware of how finite my days are. Since turning 40 in January, I’ve also experienced daily reminders of aging: inexplicable pains that rotate between my back, neck, and hips. Spiritually, I feel young; physically, my body screams otherwise. Aging is natural, but I had a creeping suspicion I could buy myself more time.

articles.title: Law Firm Linked to Elon Musk Started an ‘Election Integrity’ Organization
articles.summary: The firm that helped set up Elon Musk’s America PAC is behind the new group, which will work with election officials to pursue policies aligned with Donald Trump’s false election fraud claims.
body: The law firm that helped set up Elon Musk’s America PAC has created a new, nationwide “election integrity” organization aligned with Donald Trump’s false claims of election fraud, WIRED has learned.

The organization, a nonprofit called the Association of State and Local Election Officials, was established by a lawyer then at Lex Politica, the Musk-linked law firm founded by Chris Gober, who was chief counsel for America PAC in 2024 and is now running in Texas for a spot in the House of Representatives.

The board of directors, according to the nonprofit’s registration filing in Texas, boasts Florida secretary of state Cord Byrd, current and former state election officials in Georgia, a Michigan state representative, and the president of Cleta Mitchell’s Election Integrity Network, a Trump administration-aligned election denial group. Byrd announced his involvement with the group—which he said won’t begin until after the election—alongside Florida governor Ron DeSantis in September, as the pair touted its mission, which aims to bring what they call “election integrity” policies down to the state and local level nationwide.

articles.title: Astronomers Discover a Possible New Dwarf Planet in Our Solar System
articles.summary: Lying beyond Pluto, 2026 ED138 could be as large as 1,500 kilometers in diameter. Astronomers are still working to confirm whether it meets the criteria for a dwarf planet.
body: Scientists are on the verge of confirming the discovery of another member of the solar system, a potential dwarf planet. Astronomers at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile located the object, provisionally named 2026 ED138.

The prospective planet measures somewhere between 600 and 1,500 kilometers in diameter and is located about 46 astronomical units from the sun (an astronomical unit being Earth’s approximate distance from the sun). For comparison, Pluto —which is also now considered a dwarf planet—orbits at an average distance of 40 astronomical units. Based on its location, ED138 belongs to the population of trans-Neptunian objects. According to its discoverers, it could be one of the brightest known objects of this type and also among the largest.
Like Pluto, the possible Dwarf planet’s orbit is tilted relative to the plane on which the planets orbit.

articles.title: Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
articles.summary: On Tuesday, defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, starting with a single model in 2027.
body: Palmer Luckey says it was always the goal, and now the company is committing to it.

Even a single Made-in-USA laptop would be a surprise, because no major US computer company builds its laptops here — not Apple, not Dell, not HP, not Microsoft. We’re not aware of any company that does.

But we are aware of companies that have briefly and strategically assembled computers here seemingly to appease President Donald Trump. We’re also aware of companies that have promised US jobs only to deliver empty buildings. And we’re aware of at least one fake “US” company that lied to the government about making product domestically.

That’s why we now ask pointed questions when a company says it’s committed to US manufacturing. We asked TP-Link those sorts of questions just over a week ago. On Monday, we asked Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Qualcomm president and CEO Cristiano Amon those kinds of questions.

articles.title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s
articles.summary: Ofcom says photo and digital ID, banking checks or facial age estimation can help prove someone is 16 or over.
body: Ofcom has set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.

Under the UK's social media ban - which is due to come into force in March next year - those under that age will be prevented from accessing ten of the biggest platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
Many UK adults are also likely to have to confirm that they are not under-age by using one of the proposed measures, which are subject to government approval.
A similar ban was introduced in Australia last year but many children there have found ways to get round it. The UK says it intends to take a tougher approach.

articles.title: Investors turn on Google owner Alphabet after profit miss, ad slowdown and high spending
articles.summary: Net profit slid 25% from a year earlier to $26.2bn, well short of expectations, though revenue rose to $127.6bn. Shares in Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10% in after-hours trading Wednesday, erasing tens of billions of dollars in stock market value from the $4tn tech giant.
body: Net profit slid 25% from a year earlier to $26.2bn in the July-to-September period, or $2.12 a share, well short of expectations by analysts surveyed by FactSet.
Alphabet booked an $8.7bn loss on its equity investments, which it attributed to its stake in SpaceX, the Elon Musk-led company where shares have struggled since going public in June.
Revenue, however, rose 25% to an enormous $127.6bn. The figure was slightly below the roughly $128bn analysts had forecast.

Advertising revenue grew 11% to $82bn, short of expectations. Revenue from Google’s search business, still the company’s largest source of income, rose 12% to $63.4bn, slowing from 17% growth in the previous quarter.

articles.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
articles.summary: United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company's 2026 launch schedule into oblivion.
body: The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval.

The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA’s primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan.

Space Force officials will closely scrutinize Vulcan’s return-to-flight mission. The Pentagon has entrusted ULA’s Vulcan rocket for roughly half of its major launches through the early 2030s. The Space Force certified the Vulcan rocket for national security launches in 2025, then flew two missions on Vulcan before its grounding after the February booster incident.

articles.title: Microsoft posts $92.3bn quarterly revenue after offering buyouts to 60,000 employees
articles.summary: Software giant reports $36.6bn in profit, beating Wall Street expectations, as Azure cloud computing division grows 48%. Microsoft gained billions of dollars in stock market value Wednesday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, just days after it offered voluntary…
body: The office software giant’s growth was fueled by its Azure cloud computing division, which grew by 48% in the September quarter.
“We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost-efficiency for customers across our entire stack,” Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella said in a statement.

The technology giant recorded $92.3bn in total revenue and more than $36.6bn in profit, the company said in a securities filing Wednesday. Analysts had expected around $90.6bn in revenue and $35.1bn in profit, according to FactSet.

The quarterly earnings report comes two days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant spends heavily on artificial intelligence investments.

articles.title: As US ties fray, Europe plans first undersea cable link to Greenland
articles.summary: The European Union plans to create the first subsea Internet cable directly connecting Europe to Greenland. The Pan-Arctic Cable project could also extend to Canada and eventually link with Japan and South Korea, notably bypassing the United States.
body: The Pan-Arctic Cable is described as a European Union flagship project in a European Commission joint communication published on October 20, 2026. The policy document describes a new European strategy for the Arctic that supports “a sovereign, secure and resilient submarine cable connection linking Greenland directly to the EU,” while also suggesting that “like-minded partners like Canada” could provide a stepping stone for future cable expansion toward Asia.

“It is interesting that this project is even being considered, because five years ago it would have seemed like not a particularly commercially attractive proposition,” Elisabeth Braw, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative, told Ars. “But the fact that it's being considered is very much on trend and a sign of our times.”

articles.title: Peptide peddlers cheer as RFK Jr. unilaterally grants access, overruling FDA
articles.summary: Anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy has unilaterally passed a rule that will allow specialty pharmacies to sell six specific peptide drugs, overruling scientists at the Food and Drug Administration.
body: The peptides are popular among members of Kennedy's Make America Health Again movement and many prominent MAHA figures and Kennedy allies sell them. Kennedy said he uses some of the peptides and called himself a "big fan." But FDA scientists continue to say there is insufficient evidence to show if they're effective and they are potentially dangerous. In 2023, the safety concerns led the FDA to remove the six peptides from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies called compounding pharmacies—which make customized formulations of drugs for patients, or, in cases such as this, specialty drugs in bulk.

articles.title: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
articles.summary: The MPC Sample Key isn't even formally announced yet, but Akai is already showing off what the modding community is cooking up through vibe coding. Akai has decided to embrace the explosion of hackers and custom firmware developers by giving them early access to the device, which will have…
body: The MPC Sample Key will be an open-source 37-key take on its budget-friendly MPC Sample.

It will likely run some version of the same software found on the MPC Sample, but with tweaks to accommodate the traditional keyboard, pitch, and mod wheels. Unlike the higher-end MPC Key 37, however, the Sample Key doesn’t have pads. Instead, you play back samples with the keys.

In the short Instagram Reels posted last night and today, Akai shows a number of vibe-coded mods that add synths, including Native Instruments Massive, to the device, as well as virtual analog and FM synths. One is even shown running a completely custom OS, with “several different synths in it.”

According to the clips, the same “community” features will come to the regular MPC Sample, which is also shown running a few vibe-coded synths built by Claude. That could mean Akai plans to open-source the entire MPC Sample platform.
